reason:
The observation is measurably true and the fix is measurably wrong. Driven at 390/768/1280/1440 (state=owner-editing), .b-undo is display:flex + visibility:hidden with data-empty=true at all four, and the first label ('WHAT IT IS') sits exactly 89px below .b-edit's top edge every time (.b-edit padding-top: 88px, master.html:1200). So the band is real. It is refuted on the fix, on four independent grounds.

1. The fix breaks a passing gate assertion and reinstates the exact Round-1 defect that assertion was written to catch. interaction-check.mjs:441 reads: ok("it says nothing before anything has happened", atRest.empty === "true" && atRest.text === "", atRest.text) - measured on the OPEN editor at 1440x960, with the comment two lines above naming the paid-for defect: 'Round 1: it announced "the invitations moved seven days closer" on arrival, before anything had been touched.' Writing the committed date into .b-undoText at rest makes text !== "" and fails that gate. The finding is not spending itself past the gates; it is proposing to undo one.

2. .b-undo carries role="status" (render-b.js:492), asserted as a live region at interaction-check.mjs:439. It is built empty at mount and moved into the panel on open (moveUndoBar). Filling it on open is a live-region mutation: every screen-reader owner would hear the date announced for having done nothing. That is the same Round-1 defect in the audio channel.

3. It triplicates, and it does not even duplicate the string it claims to. The panel already carries the committed date twice inside ~120px: #b-edit-date's value is '8 August 2026' (fmt.medium + fmt.year) and .b-stepRead reads 'Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days' (fmt.longYear + dayCount). The finding says its band would carry 'the same string the readout carries'; it would not - a bare mono date at 12 is a THIRD distinct formatting of one fact, stacked above the other two. Worse, the band sits above 'What it is', so the panel would open by stating the date three times before it names the moment, inverting the hierarchy the panel deliberately leads with.

4. It is two incompatible surfaces in one 50px band. At rest it would read as a date-stamp header - and dropping visibility:hidden from .b-undo also un-hides its border-bottom hairline (master.html:1207), so the date gets a rule under it and commits harder to being a header. The instant the first +1 lands, that header is replaced by a transient 'Send the invitations moved 7 days earlier.' with a button and a Ctrl Z hint. A strip that teaches 'this is the date' and then silently becomes a toast is a worse read than a strip that is simply quiet until it has something true to say. The current design's restraint is why the void does NOT read as broken: visibility:hidden takes the hairline with it, so there is no orphan rule, nothing clipped, nothing half-drawn - it reads as generous top padding on a dark sheet, which is Linear's own idiom, not a rendering failure.

On the specific question asked: the fix does NOT introduce a focusable-but-invisible control. .b-undoAct is disabled + tabindex=-1 while empty (paintUndo, render-b.js:508-509), and an in-panel audit at all four widths returned zero invisible-focusable elements before and would return zero after. That is the one thing the fix gets right, and it is not enough to carry it.

The band itself is the last 89px of unearned space in the panel, and something quieter than a third date could earn it. But this fix trades a silent reserve for a broken gate, a spurious announcement, and a redundant third date. Refuted.
sharpenedFix: If the band is to be closed at all, do not put content in the live region - close the space instead. Reduce the reserve to the single-line height the bar actually needs at rest and let it grow only when it wraps, or move the reservation into the panel's existing top padding so the at-rest panel simply has a smaller, deliberate-looking crown. Any variant must keep .b-undoText empty and data-empty="true" until a change lands, or it fails interaction-check.mjs:441 and re-announces the Round-1 defect to screen readers.
